analysis: The only changed file in this batch is CHANGELOG.md (mode 100644, no rename or mode change), covering head lines 409 onward in two units. The units are documentation only, with no executable code, configuration or schema changes. I found no new attack surface or regression from the file itself. The entries describe behavior already tracked by the threat model: App Attest serving authorization and revocation (TB-011, T-052..T-058, A-015..A-017), the roster privacy exclusion, and SSD prefix-cache disk policy (T-041). The v0.9.0 candidate entry about a 100 GiB SSD cache ceiling is historical and was superseded by the v0.9.1 entry. That v0.9.1 entry matches the T-041 description of available-disk/2 with no fixed ceiling and a 20 GiB reserve. The changelog also does not mention the 30-minute prefix-cache TTL or the retired-cache deletion sweep that T-041 now describes. That is a documentation gap only, not a security issue in this PR. Because no source is supplied, the changelog's claims cannot be checked against code, and the next pass should confirm them against the actual coordinator and provider changes if those are in the PR. Several entries (the 0.9.9 changes, App Attest recovery and retry behavior, the CandidateCDHash binding to the durably qualified full hash) assert security-relevant behavior. Those claims are not verifiable from this batch. The T-054 build-qualification and T-053 stale-authorization properties should be reviewed in any accompanying code units.
